newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soy products end sharply higher to limit-up.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soy products end sharply higher to limit-up.

text.p: CBOT soy product markets ended sharply higher to limit up on Friday in response to bullish data from the U.S. Department of Agriculture and heavy fund buying, traders said.
"Dreyfus sold about 1,000 lots of oil late which got some attention but there was big fund buying," one pit trader said.
All nearby soyoil contracts ended at the daily 1.00 cent per pound trading limit, and May and July soymeal ended at the $10.00 daily trading limit.
Commodity funds bought at least 4,000 lots of soymeal and 7,000 lots of soyoil, pit sources said.
Ideas that lower soybean production will mean lower supplies of soyoil and soymeal prompted most of the speculative buying, traders said.

Analysts also noted that USDA lowered its U.S. soyoil yield to 10.92 pounds per bushel from a previous forecast of 11.10. Ending stocks were lowered despite a higher crushing pace because of the lower soyoil extraction rates, USDA said.
Soyoil ended up 0.15 to 1.01 cent per pound, with March up 1.00 at 24.76. Soymeal settled up $5.30 to $10.00 per ton, with March up $9.40 at $229.50.
On the day, Refco bought 2,000 lots March soymeal, Dean Witter bought 600 lots March and Tradelink bought 500 lots March.

In soyoil trading, Prudential Securities bought 1,000 lots March and 500 July. Rosenthal, Dean Witter, Griffin and Merrill Lynch each bought 1,000 lots March and ADM bought 700 March, pit sources said.

Both soymeal and soyoil will trade on expanded daily limits Monday. The trading limit in soyoil will be 1.50 cent per pound and the limit in soymeal will be $15.00 per ton, according to CBOT regulations.
Soyoil futures volume was estimated by the CBOT at 31,000 contracts, above 26,067 contracts traded Thursday.
Soymeal futures volume was estimated at 29,000 contracts, sharply above the 18,989 traded Thursday, the exchange said.
